rounds.text: Sattrix Information Security Ltd is demonstrating exceptional top-line and bottom-line momentum that significantly outpaces broader sector medians, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 36% [E16] and profit growth of 104% [E19]. This fundamental acceleration is corroborated by recent screening metrics showing a staggering 115% year-over-year sales increase alongside a 598% year-over-year net profit surge [E52, E54]. Operational efficiency is simultaneously improving, with annual operating margins expanding by 7 percentage points to reach 20% by March 2026, and quarterly operating margins spiking by 23 percentage points to 28% in the same period [E24, E25]. Furthermore, the company is almost debt-free with a minimal debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x [E31, E45], and its completed capital expenditure—evidenced by Capital Work-in-Progress dropping to zero—signals that new capacity is fully primed to come online [E34]. Insider conviction remains steadfast as promoters have actively increased their stake to 74.96% by September 2026 [E35], while the market's lagging sentiment ignores an impressive results score of 100/100 where surging profitability is dramatically outstripping 1-year price performance [E20, E43, E58]. Conceded: the company carries low return on equity metrics, including a trailing one-year ROE of 7% and a three-year median of 9% [E22, E23], alongside high debtor days reaching 234 days [E49] and a negative free cash flow of Rs -149.76 Cr as of March 2026 [E30].

Despite recent reported profit acceleration, Sattrix Information Security Ltd carries severe fundamental risks and a valuation completely unsupported by its underlying cash generation and return metrics [E39, E40]. The company features a dreadful cash conversion ratio of 0.28x for Mar 2026, meaning reported profits are heavily detached from actual cash realities and pointing directly to ballooning receivables and accruals [E28]. This cash disconnect manifests in a staggering free cash flow of Rs -149.76 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside high debtors of 234 days and a severe working capital blow-out from 85.1 days to 188 days [E30, E49, E50]. Furthermore, returns on capital are deeply sub-par with a recent ROCE of 9.6% and an ROE of 6.9%, substantially trailing sector benchmarks and highlighting inefficient capital deployment [E9, E10, E12, E13]. Institutional confidence is entirely absent, evidenced by 0.00% foreign and domestic institutional holdings, outright institutional outflow, and a negative money flow signal [E36, E37, E38, E57]. Finally, the stock offers zero dividend yield and trades at a precarious DCF intrinsic value matching its exact market price of Rs 290, leaving a margin of safety of precisely 0.0% [E4, E39, E40]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong trailing sales and profit growth alongside an operating margin expansion to 28% in Mar 2026 [E16, E19, E25].

Conceded: free cash flow stands at Rs -149.76 Cr in Mar 2026 and debtors are high at 234 days [E30, E49]. However, the bear's claim of poor fundamentals ignores explosive compounding: 5-year profit growth sits at 34% alongside a trailing twelve month profit surge of 104% [E17, E19]. Operating margins have expanded dramatically to 28% in Mar 2026 compared to just 4% in the year-ago quarter [E25]. The company remains almost debt free with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.03x, and capital-intensive buildouts are finishing as capital work in progress drops to zero [E31, E34, E45]. Conceded: institutional holding is negligible at 0.00% [E36, E37]. Yet the reverse DCF confirms that today's price of Rs 290 demands an 18.0% earnings growth rate, which matches the company's historical 3-year compounded profit growth of 27% and recent operational acceleration [E18, E39, E41, E58].

Conceded: 5-year profit growth sits at 34% alongside a trailing twelve-month profit surge of 104% and operating margins of 28% [E17, E19, E25]. However, that explosive growth fails to translate into actual cash, as evidenced by a catastrophic free cash flow of Rs -149.76 Cr and a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.28x [E28, E30]. The claim that capital-intensive buildouts are finishing ignores the staggering operational drag of high debtors at 234 days and ballooning working capital days from 85.1 to 188 days [E34, E49, E50]. Furthermore, citing a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x obscures the reality that borrowings more than tripled from Rs 1.74 Cr to Rs 6.15 Cr in a single year [E31, E33]. Finally, relying on the reverse DCF demanding 18.0% growth ignores the zero margin of safety, institutional outflow, and a low 3-year median return on equity of just 9% [E22, E37, E40, E41].
